title: Creating a Web API Project
description: Learn how to create a new ASP.NET Core Web API project.

data.text: Creating an ASP.NET Core Web API project is fast and reproducible thanks to the **.NET CLI**. Whether you prefer a terminal, Visual Studio, or VS Code, the CLI is the source of truth — the IDEs just call it for you behind the scenes.

In this lesson you will install the SDK, scaffold a project, run it, and explore the files that were created. Every later lesson builds on this foundation, so take a moment to actually run the commands yourself.

terms.definition: The Software Development Kit that contains the `dotnet` CLI, runtime, and base libraries. Download from `https://dot.net`.
Cross-platform command-line tool used to create, build, run, and publish .NET projects.
A pre-defined project skeleton. `dotnet new webapi` uses the official Web API template.
The .NET version your project compiles against (for example, `net8.0`). Set in the `.csproj` file.

data.title: Check your SDK first
data.text: Run `dotnet --version` and `dotnet --list-sdks` to confirm you have at least **.NET 8.0** installed. The Web API template and Minimal APIs we use throughout this course assume a modern SDK.

Open a terminal in the folder where you want to keep your projects, then run `dotnet new webapi`. The CLI will create a new folder with the project name, generate the standard files, and restore NuGet packages automatically.

data.title: Create and run a Web API project
data.content: Scaffold a new Web API, then run it with hot reload enabled.
data.code:
# 1. Create a new Web API project (uses Minimal API template by default)
dotnet new webapi -n MyWebApi

# 2. Move into the new folder
cd MyWebApi

# 3. Restore NuGet packages (also runs implicitly)
dotnet restore

# 4. Run with hot reload so changes auto-rebuild
dotnet watch run

data.title: Use --use-controllers for the controller template
data.text: Modern .NET SDKs default to **Minimal APIs**. If you want the classic `Controllers/` folder structure used throughout this course, pass the flag: `dotnet new webapi -n MyWebApi --use-controllers`.

rows: Generates the classic `Controllers/` template instead of Minimal APIs.

Skips HTTPS redirection for quick local experiments.

cards.title: Minimal API
cards.description: Endpoints defined inline in `Program.cs` using `app.MapGet(...)` and similar methods.
pros: Less ceremony — one file for small services
cons: Harder to organize as the API grows
Less familiar to teams coming from MVC

cards.title: Controller-based
cards.description: Endpoints defined in classes that inherit from `ControllerBase`, decorated with attributes.
pros: Strong conventions for routing, filters, and model binding
Easier to scale to dozens of endpoints
cons: More files and folders for a tiny API

data.text: This course uses the **Controller-based** template because it is the most widely deployed in production ASP.NET Core codebases and the patterns transfer directly to Minimal APIs later.

data.title: Create your first Web API
data.description: Practice the full scaffolding workflow end-to-end. Doing it once by hand cements the steps better than reading about them.
steps: Open a terminal in any folder you like.
Run `cd TodoApi && dotnet watch run` and open the printed `http://localhost:5xxx/weatherforecast` URL.
Stop the app with `Ctrl+C`, then open `Program.cs` and the `WeatherForecastController.cs` files in your editor.
Re-run the app and confirm you can see JSON output in the browser.
data.expectedOutcome: You have a working `TodoApi` project named after a real domain (todos), the default `WeatherForecast` endpoint still responds, and you know where the entry point and controllers live.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `dotnet new webapi` scaffolds a complete, runnable ASP.NET Core Web API.
Pass `--use-controllers` to get the classic MVC-style template used in this course.
`Program.cs` is the entry point and `appsettings.json` holds configuration.
`dotnet watch run` rebuilds automatically as you edit files — ideal for development.
The CLI is the source of truth: every IDE shells out to `dotnet` under the hood.
data.takeaway: Creating a Web API project is one command — `dotnet new webapi --use-controllers` — and the rest of the course is about filling in `Program.cs` and the `Controllers/` folder.
